heading: INT. FIELD KITCHEN IN A RUINED OPERA HOUSE - LATE AFTERNOON

units.text: INT. FIELD KITCHEN IN A RUINED OPERA HOUSE - LATE AFTERNOON
Plaster cherubs on the ceiling, dust on the velvet seats.
In the orchestra pit, a canvas-covered stove ticks and hisses.
A gaping hole in the roof lets a shaft of watery sunlight fall onto the stage, where a dozen mess tins steam in a row.
CAPTAIN ANNELIES DE VRIES, 40s, reading glasses pushed up into gray-blond hair, leans on a conductor's stand with a ledger.
SERGEANT IGNACY WRÓBEL, 50s, thick mustache, stirs a vat of barley soup with an oar-length spoon.
CORPORAL EZRA PRYCE, 20s, peels potatoes on the lip of the stage with excruciating care.
PRIVATE LUCIEN BEAUMONT, 19, sits in the first row with a rifle across his knees and a tin of cigarettes he is not allowed to open.
PRIVATE "DOC" SUNDARAM, 30s, a medic with a faded red cross on his sleeve, picks his way down the aisle holding a crate of tinned peaches.
The distant guns thud, soft as a bass drum in another building.
Nobody reacts.
Mess in ten minutes. Tins out, men. Boots off the seats.
units.name: DE VRIES

units.text: Beaumont lowers his boots.
Pryce nods without looking up.
Wróbel taps the spoon on the rim of the vat, the rhythm of a conductor calling an overture.
Thinner, Corporal. That peel is thick enough to roof a barn.
units.name: WRÓBEL

units.text: Sergeant, the potatoes are rotten.
units.name: PRYCE

units.text: Then peel the rotten out of them.
units.name: WRÓBEL

units.text: Doc Sundaram sets the crate on the stage, pries off a lid with his thumbnail, lifts a peach out, and sniffs it.

He glances at the captain, shrugs, and eats a piece with his fingers while Beaumont watches with open longing and Pryce holds out a hand until Doc drops a slice into it, and the sergeant pretends not to see any of it, stirring a little harder.
Best thing I've eaten since Naples.
units.name: SUNDARAM

units.text: Doc, you'll share that with the ward.
units.name: DE VRIES

units.text: Always, Captain.
units.name: SUNDARAM

units.text: She makes a mark in her ledger.
A flake of plaster drifts down from the ceiling and lands on the page.
She blows it away.
Captain, is it true there's a piano under the stage?
units.name: BEAUMONT

units.text: There is.
units.name: DE VRIES

units.text: Does anyone play?
units.name: BEAUMONT

units.text: Not since the third.
units.name: DE VRIES

units.text: I played in Kraków once. Badly.
units.name: WRÓBEL

units.text: You, Sergeant?
units.name: PRYCE

units.text: Everyone plays badly in Kraków. It is the national style.
units.name: WRÓBEL

units.text: Pryce grins into his peel.
Beaumont laughs, then covers his mouth as if it were illegal.
Somewhere far away a shell lands, long and low.
The chandelier overhead shivers, then stills.
Steady. That was ours.
units.name: DE VRIES

units.text: Always theirs when it's close.
units.name: SUNDARAM

units.text: Tins! Line up. If you can't hold a tin, hold a spoon.
units.name: WRÓBEL

units.text: They shuffle onto the stage, one after another, and form a ragged line in the weak sun.
Wróbel ladles.
Steam rises from each tin into the beam of light, and for a moment the whole ruined theater looks like a painting of a feast.
Captain, what do we do when it's over?
units.name: PRYCE

units.text: Eat.
units.name: DE VRIES

units.text: And after that?
units.name: PRYCE

units.text: After that, Corporal, we peel more potatoes.
units.name: DE VRIES
